# Caribe (01, engineer) — SPD-042

## Brief
Objective: zsh's SHORT_LOOPS forms, on by default, run a loop body without `do` and `done`, and ShellWalk reads that body as header words and discards it, so a member's git write, spud call, tee, cd or redirection inside `repeat N cmd`, `repeat N (list)`, `for f (a b) cmd` and the sibling short forms is never checked (Laws 1, 5, 7). Make ShellWalk read a short-loop body as what zsh runs: every command in it analysed inside a loop frame (loop_depth, as a do…done body is), the header still skipped, and the frame closed where zsh closes it, so the directory and variable model after the loop is the same as for the long form. zsh only: bash 3.2 rejects every one of these forms. Red-first.

The hole (Bintje's proposal from SPD-039; `spud ticket show SPD-042` has the evidence): in bin/spud_ledger.py ShellWalk.add_word pushes a loop frame with `skip = True` on `for`, `select` and `repeat`, and every word up to `do` is header; in ShellWalk.walk a `(` read while `skip` is set is taken for a `for (( … ))` arithmetic header and glued into one word. So `repeat 3 echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md`, `repeat 1 (echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md)` and `for f (a b) echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md` are read as header and discarded: analyse_command records no redirect and no finding, for a `**` member and for Spud. `for f in a b; echo x > ledger/…` is read today only because the `;` ends the header (finish clears skip) while the loop frame stays open to the end of the line, and `foreach f (a b) …; end` is read because foreach is not a reserved word in add_word.

Settle with real-shell probes (zsh 5.9 `-f`, and `zsh -f -o nobareglobqual` as this Mac's Bash tool runs; bash 3.2 as the control that rejects each form; in the scratchpad, with a fake `git` first on a scratch PATH and a marker file, never a real git write) and pin each with a test:
1. The grammar, from `man zshmisc` (Complex Commands; Alternate Forms For Complex Commands) confirmed by probe: what the body is after `repeat word`, `for name ( word … )`, `for name in word …;` (a term without do), `select name ( word … )` and `select name in word …;`: a `do … done`, a `{ list }`, a `( list )` subshell, or a single sublist (one and-or list or pipeline, so in `repeat 3 git push; echo x` git push runs three times and echo once, while `repeat 3 echo x | cat` and `repeat 3 true && git push` are whole sublists). Whether a newline may stand between the header and the body. Whether `for f (a b); cmd` and `repeat 3; cmd` are short loops or something else. `for (( i=0; i<3; i++ )) { … }` and `for (( … )) cmd` if zsh takes them. A `repeat` count that is a variable, an expansion or a glob. Decide each reading; where zsh's two option sets differ, the hook takes the reading that runs.
2. What runs inside: a git write verb (Law 7), a spud call under `--as spud` or with another member's actor (Laws 5 and 6), tee and cd the hook tracks, and a redirection into ledger/ or a path outside the member's deliverables (Laws 1 and 5), each inside every body form of item 1, for the `**` member, a narrow-glob member and Spud. Spud is never refused for git; check his reading against the checks that apply to him (Law 5 `--as` another actor, the database, the hook, Law 1 through tee or a redirection).
3. The loop model: a relative `cd` in a short-loop body may repeat, so it is unfollowable as in a do…done body (loop_depth); after the loop the directories are the union of before and after, as pop computes for the long form; a `cd x` after the sublist ends is outside the loop and followed. The loop variable of `for name (…)` and `select name (…)` is doubted as SPD-043 does for the long form, so `for X (git) $X push` and `for X in git; $X push` are refused for a member. A short loop nested in a long one and the reverse; a short loop inside `{ }`, `( )`, a function body, `eval '…'`, `sh -c` and `zsh -c` strings, a command substitution and a coproc; two short loops on one line; a short loop whose sublist holds `&&`, `||`, `|` and a trailing `&`.
4. Controls that keep today's reading, each pinned: `for f in a b; do …; done`, `for f in a b` newline `do` newline `…` newline `done`, `for (( i=0; i<3; i++ )); do …; done`, `select f in a b; do …; done`, `while …; do …; done`, `until`, `repeat 3; do …; done`, `foreach f (a b); …; end`, `case`, `name () { … }`, `function name { … }`, `name=(a b)` arrays, `(cmd)` subshells, `for`, `repeat` and `select` as ordinary arguments (`echo repeat 3`, `git log --grep 'for f (a b)'`, `grep -n repeat file`), the same forms quoted inside strings, and every existing test.

Out of scope: `if list sublist` and `while list { list }` (read today; pin one control each and leave them), SPD-054's trap strings (another session, on its own branch: do not touch analyse_segment's trap branch or EFFECT_ORDER), SPD-055's wrapper assignments, SPD-059's aliases, SPD-060's named coproc, redirections into digit-named files (SPD-045), bash-only `for name; do` without `in` and other bash spellings unless the fix covers them for free. ## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: a zsh short if, while or until with a [[ ]] condition hides its body** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-061]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: zsh's SHORT_LOOPS also give if, while and until a body with no then/do, and when the condition is a [[ ... ]] test the hook reads the whole line as one simple command whose command word is [[, so the body's git verb, spud call or command word is never checked (Law 7, Laws 5 and 6). SPD-042 fixed the for, select and repeat forms; this is the same hole in the sibling forms, and the ticket named them out of scope on the belief that they were read today. They are not. zsh runs them; bash 3.2 rejects each.
  Evidence: Probed zsh 5.9 -f and -o nobareglobqual in the scratchpad with a fake git first on PATH: 'if [[ -n x ]] git push' pushed once; 'n=0; while [[ $((n++)) -lt 2 ]] git push' and the same with a { git push } body pushed twice; 'n=0; until [[ $((n++)) -ge 2 ]] git push' pushed twice. bash 3.2 gave a syntax error for each. On SPD-042's branch analyse_command records findings=[] for all four (the redirect target is still captured, the verb is not). The forms that do work today: 'if (( 1 )) git push' and 'while (( n < 2 )) git push' are read, because (( )) splits into subshell frames; 'if true git push' and 'if true; git push' are zsh parse errors, so only the [[ ]] spelling leaks. Fix sketch: in ShellWalk, let ']]' end an if/while/until condition the way SPD-042's end_header ends a loop header, then reuse resolve_body and close_sublists.

## Result
Produced (worktree spd-042-zsh-short-loops, uncommitted): bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only.

THE FIX. A zsh short loop body is now analysed as what zsh runs: every command in it inside the loop frame (loop_depth), the header still skipped, the frame closed where zsh closes it.
- ShellFrame gains `body`: "header" while a for, select or repeat header is read, "pending" until the body's first word, then "long" (`do ... done`), "compound" (a `{ ... }` or `( ... )` body that closes the loop with it) or "sublist" (one and-or list, closing the loop where that list ends).
- ShellWalk gains `header` ("for", "repeat", "func"), `expect_body`, and open_loop / end_header / resolve_body / close_sublists. The header ends after repeat's one word, at the `)` of `for name ( ... )` and `for (( ... ))`, or at the `;` or newline of the `in` and positional forms; close_sublists runs at `;`, `;;`, `&`, `)`, `}`, `fi`, `done`, `esac` and at the end of the line, and pop() chains a compound body's frame into its loop. A repeat count no longer doubts the names in it (it assigns nothing); a for or select header still does, so the loop variable stays doubted.
- `coproc`, `time` and `!` may stand before a loop keyword (LOOP_PREFIX_WORDS), and the `name ()` function-header branch no longer fires inside a header, so `for f () cmd` is a loop.
- mark_zsh_patterns: a for or select word list's parentheses are punctuation, not a glob group, with command position restored after the closing `)`; a `for (( ... ))` header restores it too, and so does the word after `repeat`. So `for f (a b) (git push)` and `repeat 1 (git push)` open subshells, and these lines now have one reading where they had two.

DECISIONS, each with its probe (zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual = this Mac's Bash tool, bash 3.2 as the control that rejects every form; scratchpad only, a fake git first on a scratch PATH writing a marker file). 142 probes ran under both zsh option sets and none differed, so there was no reading to choose between.
1. Header. `repeat word` takes exactly one word, arithmetic-evaluated: `repeat 1+1`, `n=2; repeat $n` and `repeat $(echo 2)` each ran twice, and `repeat ?` with a file named 2 in the directory ran nothing, so the count is not globbed. Also `for name ( word ... )`, `for name in word ... TERM`, `for name TERM` (the positional parameters), `select` in both spellings, and `for (( ... ))`. TERM is `;` or a newline and more than one may stand between a header and its body (`repeat 2 ;\n;\n git push` pushed twice). `for f in a b do ...` is a parse error, so the `in` form always has a terminator before its body. `for f (a|b)` is a parse error, so a loop's word list is never a glob; `for f ()` is valid and runs nothing.
2. Body. A `do ... done`, a `{ list }`, a `( list )` subshell, or one sublist: the whole and-or list with its pipelines (`repeat 2 echo a | wc -l` printed 1 twice, so the pipeline is inside; `repeat 3 true && git push` and `repeat 3 false || git push` pushed three times), a compound command (`repeat 2 if true; then git push; fi` and `repeat 2 case x in x) git push;; esac` pushed twice), and each command's redirections. It ends at `;`, a newline or `&`: `repeat 2 echo a >> f1; echo b >> f2` left two lines in f1 and one in f2, and `repeat 2 git push & wait` pushed twice, so `&` ends the body and backgrounds the whole loop.
3. Directories. The loop runs in the shell itself: `repeat 1 cd d; pwd`, `for f (a) cd d; pwd`, `for (( i=0; i<1; i++ )) cd d; pwd` and `repeat 1 { cd d }` all ended in d, and `repeat 1 (cd d)` did not. So a relative cd in a short body is unfollowable (loop_depth) and a member's later relative target is refused; an absolute one leaves the union of before and after, as pop computes for `do ... done`; a `( )` body's cd does not carry out; and a cd after the sublist is outside the loop and followed (`repeat 1 true; cd d; pwd` ended in d).
4. Context. zsh runs a short loop inside `{ }`, `( )`, a function body, `eval`, `zsh -c`, `$( )`, backticks, and after `coproc`, `time` and `!`; `nocorrect repeat`, `noglob repeat`, `command repeat` and `- repeat` are a parse error or look for a program named repeat, so those prefixes are left alone.
5. The loop variable of `for name (...)` and `select name (...)` is doubted, so `for X (git) $X push` and `for X in git; $X push` are refused for a member (SPD-043's var-doubt); zsh ran git push in both.

TESTS, red first. ZshShortLoopTest, 12 methods, placed right after ShellModelTest. Against a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin it fails 10 of 12 with 212 failures; the two that pass are the control methods, which pin today's reading. Coverage: the ticket's three evidence commands for the ** member, the tests/** member and Spud; 19 header forms; 10 body forms; Law 7, Law 6 (`ticket new` and `--as spud`), Law 5's `--as` another actor, the database, tee and a ledger redirection in four body forms for all three callers, plus a target outside a narrow member's deliverables; the loop model; the loop variable; nesting and every enclosing context; the sublist boundary; bounded time on deep nesting; and the controls (the long forms of for, select, while, until, repeat, foreach, case, functions, arrays, subshells, `repeat`/`for`/`select` as ordinary and quoted words, `git log --grep 'for f (a b) git push'`). Whole suite from the worktree: Ran 678 tests, OK (666 before).

VERIFIED BEYOND TESTS. Hook-level differential: 2667 command lines (every string in tests/test_hooks.py under 300 characters whose in-process reading changed, plus a 600-line sample of those that did not) run through PreToolUse(Bash) for the ** member, the tests/** member and Spud, against the unchanged bin and against the branch: 0 deny to not-deny. 1524 silent-or-allow became deny (the bodies now checked) and 205 denials kept a different, more specific reason (188 of them a var refusal becoming Law 7); no Law 7 refusal was lost. Structural differential over 8253 strings (the same corpus plus a generated grid of 30 headers by 13 bodies by 13 payloads and 8 pathological inputs): 2079 read differently, 0 redirect targets and 0 candidate directories lost, and the 94 lines whose finding kind changed are all the same pattern, a var refusal becoming a git finding plus var-doubt because the assignment inside the body is now read. Deep nesting is bounded: 2000 nested short loops, 500 nested brace bodies, 200 nested subshell bodies and a 20000-word for list each stay under 0.05 s and still find the git push.

LATENCY, PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15, interleaved with a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin on one scratch home with one bound member: plain command 23.1 to 23.1 ms (silent both); long-form loop 23.1 to 23.3 ms (silent both); short-form loop with a git write 23.3 to 23.6 ms (silent before, deny now).

PROPOSAL 64 (P1), held by Spud: a zsh short `if`, `while` or `until` with a `[[ ... ]]` condition still hides its body. The ticket put `if list sublist` and `while list { list }` out of scope believing they were read today; `while (( ... )) cmd` is, but `if [[ -n x ]] git push`, `while [[ ... ]] git push`, `while [[ ... ]] { git push }` and `until [[ ... ]] git push` all run in zsh while the hook reads the line as one simple command whose command word is `[[`, with no finding. `if true git push` and `if true; git push` are zsh parse errors, so only the `[[ ]]` spelling leaks.

LIMITS. `sh -c 'repeat 1 git push'` is refused although sh has no `repeat`: one analyser reads every shell string. A zsh `{ list }` whose `}` has no terminator before it still keeps that `}` as a word of the last command; the directory set that follows is a superset of the real one, so it over-refuses and never under-refuses. `foreach ... end` keeps its pre-SPD-042 reading, as the ticket asked. ## Outcome
ShellWalk now reads a zsh short-loop body (do…done, { list }, ( list ) or one sublist) inside the loop frame with the header skipped and the frame closed where zsh closes it: ShellFrame.body with open_loop, end_header, resolve_body and close_sublists, LOOP_PREFIX_WORDS for coproc, time and !, and mark_zsh_patterns no longer reading a for or select word list as a glob group. ZshShortLoopTest, 12 methods, 212 failures red first; suite 678 OK on the branch. A hook-level differential of 2667 lines for three callers lost no denial, a structural one over 8253 strings lost no target or directory, and latency moved at most 0.3 ms. 142 probes under both zsh option sets never differed. Proposal 64 (a short if, while or until with a [[ ]] condition) becomes its own ticket.
